title: From Blah to Blaze: Spark Motivation When You Feel Stuck
description: Feeling stuck and flat? Here's the simple approach: start smaller than feels respectable, use your inspiration fix, and move your body before you overthink it.
excerpt: Start small, use your inspiration fix, and move before you overthink it.

blocks.text: Stuck doesn't usually feel dramatic. It feels flat. You're not in crisis. You're just going through the motions, and every plan quietly slides to next week. Here's the simple answer: the way out isn't a bigger plan. It's a smaller one, done today.

blocks.heading: Start smaller than feels respectable
blocks.text: When you're flat, ambition gets in the way. A five-day plan you can't start is still nothing. Shrink it until it's almost embarrassing: one paragraph, one email, ten minutes, one room. The point isn't impressive output. It's proving you can still move when you decide to.

blocks.heading: Find your inspiration fix
blocks.text: Most people already know what turns the lights back on. A certain album. A walk on a certain route. One friend who talks straight. Write yours down. When the fire dips, you don't want to search for it. You want to reach for it.

blocks.heading: Move your body first, think second
items: Ten minutes walking outside beats an hour deciding indoors.
Do something physical before something mental. Order matters more than intensity.
Change the room. Stuck is often just the same chair for too long.
Clear one small mess. Clear surfaces, clearer head.

blocks.heading: Then let it be unimpressive
blocks.text: The first day back won't feel like a blaze. It feels like a spark you have to protect. Do the small thing. Notice that you did it. Do it again tomorrow. The fire comes from repetition, not from the first match.

items.q: What if the small version feels pointless?
items.a: It is pointless as a finish line. It's useful as a start. You're rebuilding the habit of moving, not finishing the whole project in one sitting.

items.q: How long until I feel motivated again?
items.a: Usually after you've already started a few times, not before. Waiting to feel ready is how the flat week becomes a flat month.
